must_remember: The Compton wavelength shift $\Delta \lambda$ depends solely on the scattering angle $\theta$ and is completely independent of the initial wavelength $\lambda$ and the scattering material.
The numerical value of the Compton wavelength $\lambda_c = \frac{h}{m_0 c}$ is approximately $2.426 \text{ pm}$ or $0.02426 \text{ \AA}$.
The maximum wavelength shift $\Delta \lambda_{\max} = 2\lambda_c$ occurs at a backscattering angle of $\theta = 180^\circ$.
The Compton effect provides direct experimental proof that photons possess momentum $p = \frac{h}{\lambda}$ and behave like particles in elastic collisions.
Visible light does not exhibit a measurable Compton shift because the photon energy is extremely small compared to the rest mass energy of an electron.

glossary.meaning: The characteristic constant length scale representing the wavelength shift, given by $\frac{h}{m_0 c} \approx 2.426 \text{ pm}$.
The angle through which the incident high-frequency photon (X-ray or gamma ray) is deflected upon collision.
The angle at which the struck electron recoils relative to the incident photon direction, determined using relativistic momentum and energy conservation.
A spectral line in scattering experiments corresponding to photons scattered by tightly bound inner-shell electrons where the entire atom recoils, rendering the effective mass extremely large.
